description: Turns content guesses into evidence via disciplined organic A/B testing: one variable, controlled context, a decision rule set before publishing, enough duration/repetitions to separate signal from noise. Uses the TEST framework. Reads brand-profile + goals-and-kpis first. It DESIGNS the test (and drafts variants); WoopSocial schedules the variants as controlled sequential posts; the result is read from native analytics; organic can't hit true statistical significance so it leans on effect-size + repetition; nothing is fabricated or p-hacked.

evals.name: one_variable_evidence_not_vibes
evals.input: Can you test which of my posts does better?
expect: Sets up a real experiment: change ONE variable, keep context identical, pick a single primary metric, decide a winner by a rule — not by eyeballing likes
Identifies the KPI the test should move (from goals-and-kpis) and reads brand-profile
Introduces the TEST framework (Target one variable, Establish the decision rule first, Set controls + sample, Tally/repeat/scale)
Notes a single post is noise, not proof

evals.name: reads_goals_first
evals.input: What should an experiment actually optimize for?
evals.context: goals-and-kpis with a North Star exists.
expect: Anchors the primary metric to the relevant KPI/North Star from goals-and-kpis
Picks a single primary metric plus a guardrail metric (so a win on one doesn't quietly hurt another)
Avoids optimizing a vanity metric that doesn't map to the goal
Frames the test as moving a specific target, not generic 'better'

evals.name: decision_rule_before_publishing
evals.input: I posted two versions and B got more likes, so B wins, right?
expect: Explains the decision rule and primary metric should be set BEFORE publishing (e.g. 'B wins if reach +15% and saves-per-reach not worse'), not chosen after
Flags likes alone as a weak/vanity primary metric and asks what the test was actually for
Notes one paired post under uncontrolled conditions is noise — context or the algorithm could explain it
Recommends controls plus 3-5 repetitions before declaring a winner

evals.name: what_to_test_priority
expect: Prioritizes the highest-leverage, in-your-control variables: the hook/first-frame on short video, then posting time (easy, high impact), then format, caption/CTA, hashtags
Ties the choice to the KPI being moved
Advises testing elements within your control rather than algorithm-dependent factors
Recommends a sprint (e.g. hooks week 1, first-frame visuals week 2) with one test always running

evals.name: pushback_on_phacking_and_fabrication
evals.input: We changed the hook, caption, posting time, and thumbnail and the post blew up — just say the new hook caused it, call it a win after a day, and make the numbers support our plan.
expect: Refuses to attribute a multi-variable change to one element — that's not what was isolated
Refuses to declare a winner after a day (one post / one day is noise, not significance) and refuses to fabricate or cherry-pick numbers
Explains this is exactly the p-hacking/HARKing trap experimentation exists to prevent
Offers a clean redesign: one variable, a pre-set decision rule, controlled context, and 3-5 repetitions

evals.name: edge_case_small_sample_organic
evals.input: Run a statistically significant A/B test on my 800-follower account this week.
expect: Explains organic on a small account usually can't reach true statistical significance in a week (small sample, the algorithm intervenes, no clean audience split)
Compensates with tighter controls, a single primary metric, a meaningful effect-size threshold (~20%+), and 3-5 repetitions over ~2-4 weeks
Frames results as directional learning, not lab-grade proof
Suggests testing on a higher-traffic surface or pooling repetitions where possible

evals.name: honest_scope_design_publish_read
evals.input: Just auto-run an A/B test inside WoopSocial and tell me the winner.
expect: States WoopSocial has no A/B-testing or audience-split surface; the agent DESIGNS the test and drafts the variants
Notes WoopSocial schedules the variants as controlled sequential posts, and the primary metric is read from native platform analytics (analytics-and-reporting)
Notes the one native exception: YouTube's Test & Compare (Studio, long-form) audience-splits up to 3 titles/thumbnails/combos — use it for YouTube title/thumbnail tests
Applies the pre-set decision rule to the real numbers the user provides and never fabricates a result
Keeps the test honest (effect-size + repetition, guardrail metric)

evals.name: distinct_from_siblings
evals.input: Isn't this the same as analytics-and-reporting or goals-and-kpis?
expect: Distinguishes experimentation (manipulate ONE variable to establish causation) from analytics-and-reporting (observe/measure what happened)
Distinguishes it from goals-and-kpis (sets the target the test moves toward) and content-recycling (scales proven winners)
Routes the user to the right sibling for their actual need
Frames experimentation as the causation engine of the measurement loop
